methodology: Two kinds of entries, distinguished by source_category: 'permit' entries are hand-transcribed from a state/federal agency's own permit or registration list (a captured_at snapshot, not a live feed). 'operational_evidence' entries are NOT permits -- they're derived from this Observatory's own already-ingested NHTSA SGO incident filings and Waymo's S2 mileage data, and exist because permit rosters alone understate real footprint: a company can genuinely operate in a state with no public permit list at all (confirmed for Texas and Georgia, for example) -- an early version of this registry wrongly showed only 4 states for Waymo because it relied on permit rosters exclusively. 'No public roster found' for a state does NOT mean no permits exist there; see states_status_notes for confirmed real-but-unpublished permit requirements vs. no AV-specific regime at all.

states_status_notes.note: Senate Bill 2807 (89th Legislature, 2025) created a MANDATORY TxDMV authorization for commercial automated-vehicle operation in Texas, enforceable since May 28, 2026 (90 days after final implementing rules took effect Feb 27, 2026). TxDMV can issue/revoke authorizations and provides a law-enforcement-only tool to verify a vehicle's authorization status, but publishes no public roster of authorization holders. This corrects an earlier, now-outdated assessment that Texas had no AV-specific permit regime -- it does, as of 2026, and it is actively enforced.

Nevada DMV requires an Autonomous Vehicle Testing Registry application (form OBL-326) and a separate Autonomous Vehicle Certification Registry for operation (form OBL-326A) -- a real permit regime with real applicants -- but no public roster of current holders was found; would require a direct records request to DMV.
Ohio requires registration with DriveOhio (created/reauthorized by executive order) before testing AVs on public roads, but no public roster of registrants was found.

Florida law (2019) opened the door to AV operation and FLHSMV has titling/registration procedures for AVs, but it's unclear whether there's a distinct AV-specific permit beyond standard vehicle registration, and no public roster was found; FLHSMV's own guidance suggests company-level detail would require a public records request.

Georgia has ADS-specific statute and real Waymo/other operations (confirmed via this Observatory's SGO and Waymo S2 data), but no state permit roster was found -- unclear whether Georgia operates a permit regime at all versus general statutory authorization.
